title: Term 1 and 2 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 1 and 2.
This question paper consists of 6 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Finance: Financial Documents, Tariffs and Budgets

questions.prompt: Which document records what was actually earned and spent last month?
Which of these is usually a fixed monthly expense?
A household has a deficit when its expenditure is greater than its income.
The same municipality first subtracts a rebate of R250 000 from the valuation. Calculate the new monthly rates on the R1 450 000 property (0,0098 per rand per year), correct to the nearest cent.
A family spends R6 800 a month on groceries. Food inflation is expected to be 6,5%. How much should they budget per month for groceries next year?
A household budgeted R3 600 for petrol but spent R4 110. By what percentage did they overspend? Round to one decimal place.

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Finance: Business Costs, Income and Break-even

questions.prompt: Which is a fixed cost for a bakery?
A shop buys a kettle for R240 and adds a 45% mark-up. What is the selling price?
Fixed costs are R5 000 and each item costs R30 to make. Calculate the total cost of making 200 items.
Fixed costs are R4 800; each item costs R20 to make and sells for R50. How many items must be sold to break even?
Selling fewer items than the break-even quantity results in a loss.
Using the T-shirt example (fixed costs R3 000, R55 per shirt, selling price R120), calculate the profit or loss if 35 T-shirts are sold.
A food stall has fixed costs of R1 500 per month and makes a profit of R12 on each meal sold. Write a formula for monthly profit $P$ for $n$ meals.
Annual gross income is R280 000 and pension contributions are R21 000. What is the taxable income?
Which document shows an employee's annual income and the tax deducted by the employer?
Calculate the total monthly UIF paid into the fund (employee plus employer) for a worker earning R9 800.
questions.memo:
✓ Employee 1% = R98 (1)
✓ Total with employer R196 (1)

questions.prompt: Explain how contributing to a pension fund can reduce the tax a person pays.
questions.memo:
✓ Pension contributions are deducted from income (1)
✓ so the taxable income, and therefore the tax, is lower (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: Finance: Investments, Loans and Inflation

questions.prompt: Calculate the simple interest on R15 000 at 6,5% p.a. for 3 years.
R10 000 is invested at 8% p.a. compounded annually. What is it worth after 3 years (two decimals)?
R5 000 is invested at 9% p.a. compounded monthly for 1 year. Calculate the final amount (two decimals).
A R20 000 loan is repaid with 24 instalments of R1 050. What is the cost of credit?
If inflation is higher than the interest earned, the buying power of savings decreases.
Name TWO costs, besides interest, that can increase the real cost of a loan.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): initiation fee; monthly service fee; credit life insurance; penalties for late payment

questions.prompt: An investment earns 9% p.a. while inflation is 5,5%. Estimate the real rate of growth and explain what it means.
questions.memo:
✓ About 3,5% (1)
✓ The buying power of the money grows by about 3,5% per year (1)

A bank sells euros at R20,40 and charges 2% commission. Calculate the cost of buying €300.

Find the surface area of a closed box 10 cm × 6 cm × 4 cm.

Give TWO reasons why a company might choose a rectangular box rather than a cylinder for cereal.
